newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil steady, first summer Russian on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil steady, first summer Russian on Sunday.

text.p: NWE fuel oil barges were lifted on Wednesday by pre-holiday bunker demand but little else moved the market, traders said.
Barges traded at $82 prompt and $82.50 first half May with bunker demand variously reported to be from 10,000 tonnes to 30,000 tonnes.
"I think a lot of traders will work on Friday but most of the majors will take two days off so a lot of guys want to get business done by the end of today," said one trader.
No cracked cargo activity was heard and low sulphur European straight-run markets were quiet.
Russian straight-run cargoes were still relatively scarce in the Baltics, with market players awaiting the arrival of the first of the summer river shipments.

River ice on the Volga had delayed until Sunday barges that had been due to arrive in St Petersburg on Thursday, one Russian trader said. The barges were travelling in convoy, preceded by a river ice breaker, he added.

Russian river-borne export volumes are expected to be sharply up this year, at between 4.25 and 4.50 million tonnes from St. Peterburg alone, a Western trader based at the port told Reuters on Wednesday.
With shipments from two smaller ports the total could hit 5.5 million tonnes, he added, an amount that will weigh heavily on the already depressed European fuel oil market.
Last year's exports were hindered by low water levels in rivers, which should not be repeated this year, the trader said.
Another factor behind the expected rise in fuel oil exports is the return to full production at the vast Norsi oil refinery in Nizhni Novgorod where output fell 27 percent from 1995 levels last year.
